newsitem.title: USA: US temporarily shuts embassy in Central Africa.
newsitem.headline: US temporarily shuts embassy in Central Africa.

text.p: Clashes between rebels and peacekeepers in the Central African Republic have prompted the United States to suspend operations temporarily at its embassy there, the State Department said on Friday.

"The United States has decided to suspend temporarily its operations in the Central African Republic in light of hostilities between rebel forces and African peacekeepers," spokesman John Dinger told reporters.

U.S. Ambassador Mosina Jordan and another embassy staff member will cover events in the Central African Republic from the U.S. embassy in Cameroon, Dinger said, but the U.S. government will not be able to give direct protection to U.S. citizens during the shutdown.
The government of France has promised to assist the American community in case of emergency.

There were about 50 U.S. citizens in the Central African Republic as of Friday, Dinger said, most of them based in the capital of Bangui. About half of those, including the embassy staff, will leave this weekend or early next week.

The immediate cause of the U.S. decision was a rocket exchange between peacekeepers and rebels last weekend, according to Dinger. West African mediators are in the Central African Republic trying to restore order, he said.
"Nevertheless there have been violent episodes and they have claimed innocent lives and although Americans are not the object of these attacks, they're clearly in danger," he said.
